subject: Tarvis Ulain
fact: Tarvis Ulain was a paladin of Bahamut who died three years ago in Daggerford while breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation. His severed bronze forearm is mounted on a stone pillar as a monument, with a Dwarven inscription reading 'The move is yours' and a Common inscription signed by Milo Goodbarrel of the Order of the Gauntlet.
source_quote: The primary text told us this was Tarvis Ulain, paladin, dead three years. Died here, in Daggerford itself, breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.

subject: Milo Goodbarrel
fact: Milo Goodbarrel is the head of a publisher and a member of the Order of the Gauntlet who personally witnessed and recorded the monument to Tarvis Ulain, signing the Common inscription on its back.
source_quote: Signed by Milo Goodbarrel, apparently head of some publisher, apparently Order of the Gauntlet. Milo had personally signed off on this.

subject: Metalworkers Guild
fact: The Metalworkers Guild funded the monument to Tarvis Ulain two years after the war, despite the presence of a Stroudite inscription, indicating possible internal ideological diversity or deliberate tolerance.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild.

subject: Order of the Gauntlet
fact: The Order of the Gauntlet commissioned and recorded the monument to Tarvis Ulain, and now sells pewter replicas of his hand as charitable donations, with a priest of Bahamut acting as their local representative in Daggerford.
source_quote: Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet. Signed by Milo Goodbarrel... He was selling them for donations to the Order of the Gauntlet.

subject: Cult of the Dragon
fact: The Cult of the Dragon was actively recruiting in Daggerford at the time of Tarvis Ulain’s death, prompting his intervention and eventual demise.
source_quote: breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.

subject: Daggerford
fact: Daggerford is a town that avoided the worst of the post-war Uthgardt barbarian hordes but suffered the presence of the Cult of the Dragon and the death of Tarvis Ulain, leaving behind a monument that has become a focal point of ideological tension and quiet remembrance.
source_quote: Daggerford had people. Daggerford had walls, and a market square, and smoke from cook fires... Only lost Tarvis.

subject: River Shining Tavern
fact: The River Shining Tavern is the local inn in Daggerford where the party arrives after encountering the monument to Tarvis Ulain and the priest selling pewter hand casts.
source_quote: We found the River Shining Tavern and noted it for later.

subject: Bronze forearm monument
fact: A bronze-cast severed forearm, mounted on a stone pillar, commemorates Tarvis Ulain. It bears a Dwarven inscription 'The move is yours,' a Common inscription signed by Milo Goodbarrel, and is associated with the Order of the Gauntlet and the Metalworkers Guild.
source_quote: a bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar... The primary text told us this was Tarvis Ulain... Dwarven, on the base. *The move is yours.*

subject: Pewter hand casts
fact: Small, charm-sized pewter reproductions of Tarvis Ulain’s severed forearm are being sold by a village priest as donations to the Order of the Gauntlet, despite their diminutive size and the ideological ambiguity of the monument’s inscription.
source_quote: carrying a tray of small pewter reproductions of Tarvis's hand cast, miniature things, charm-sized. He was selling them for donations to the Order of the Gauntlet.

subject: death of Tarvis Ulain
fact: Tarvis Ulain died three years ago in Daggerford while dismantling a Cult of the Dragon recruitment effort, an act that made him a martyr and led to the creation of a controversial monument.
source_quote: Died here, in Daggerford itself, breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.

subject: Stroudite inscription on Bahamutian monument
fact: A Dwarven inscription referencing Stroud — 'The move is yours' — appears on a monument to a Bahamutian paladin, creating unspoken tension between factions, with no one certain whether it was an oversight, a gift, or a quiet act of defiance.
source_quote: The inscription shares language with Stroud... Somebody had put a Stroudite inscription on a monument to a Bahamutian paladin... they had either not noticed or not cared enough to remove it.

subject: identity of the monument's commissioner
fact: The origin of the monument’s design — particularly the inclusion of the Stroudite inscription — remains unexplained, with the Metalworkers Guild’s possible Stroudite members and the priest’s admission that it was 'a gift' leaving the true motive ambiguous.
source_quote: It was a gift... we decided the inscription could remain.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a half-orc cleric of Bahamut who observes the monument to Tarvis Ulain with deep attention, questions its contradictions, purchases a pewter hand cast, and presses the priest for answers, demonstrating both faith and skepticism.
source_quote: Grygum made a sound when he got to the part confirming Tarvis had served Bahamut... Grygum dropped a gold piece in for his... Grygum asked him to tell him more...

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a dwarf who reads the Dwarven inscription on the monument with linguistic precision, recognizes its connection to Stroud’s chess reference, and confirms its accuracy due to his native fluency in Dwarven.
source_quote: Daz was already reading the inscription... Dwarven is, you know, actually my language, or one of them, and I wanted to make sure I hadn't misread. I hadn't.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a Dragonborn who approaches the monument with suspicion, treating it as a potential threat and questioning whether it constitutes art, reflecting his cautious, combat-oriented worldview.
source_quote: Zalthir looked at it the way he looks at most things: like he was deciding whether it constituted a threat. 'This is art?' he said.

subject: Priest of the River Shining
fact: A village priest of Bahamut sells pewter hand casts of Tarvis Ulain’s severed forearm as donations to the Order of the Gauntlet, claims purity of faith, acknowledges the Stroudite inscription as a 'gift' left in place, and adapts quickly to the diverse party’s presence.
source_quote: He himself was, he wanted us to know, *a pure Bahamutian*. He did not believe in the heresy... 'It was a gift'... He pivoted and addressed the general group with renewed energy.

subject: three years ago
fact: Tarvis Ulain died three years ago, and the monument was funded two years after the war, placing the events of Daggerford’s memorialization within a narrow post-conflict window.
source_quote: dead three years... funded two years after the war.

subject: arrival of the party in Daggerford
fact: The party arrives in Daggerford after a long journey from the Silver Marches, encountering a monument laden with ideological ambiguity and a priest selling relics, marking the beginning of their engagement with the town’s quiet, unresolved war trauma.
source_quote: Daggerford was the first place we'd walked into in weeks where the silence didn't make sense... We found the River Shining Tavern and noted it for later.
